# JVM fixtures

These classfiles are self-authored and generated byte-exactly by
[fixtures.cjs](../../jvm/fixtures.cjs). No external test corpus is copied.
The generator uses only Node's standard library; Node is
a development/test tool, not a dependency of a compiled Moss executable.

```powershell
& 'C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe' `
    'C:\Source\Moss\tests\jvm\fixtures.cjs' `
    'C:\Source\Moss\tests\fixtures\jvm'
```

| Fixture | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `Example8/17/21/25.class` | Equivalent inventories at major versions 52, 61, 65, 69 |
| `Preview.class` | Explicit Java 25 preview policy |
| `Unicode.class` | Unicode internal/method names and UTF-8 CLI selection |
| `WeirdNames.class` | Lossless NUL/surrogate code units and index-based method selection |
| `ConstantKinds.class` | All ordinary supported constant kinds, raw numeric bits, MUTF-8, bootstrap references |
| `Module.class` | Module/package constants and bounded module metadata |
| `OpcodeMatrix.class` | Every allowed base opcode, all modern wide forms, and switch alignment residues |
| `constants.json`, `opcodes.json` | Independent fixture metadata for exact assertions |
| `Example8/17/21/25.javap.txt`, `OpcodeMatrix.javap.txt` | Output of `javap -c -p -l` (JDK 25, CRs removed) for those classes; `moss disasm` must equal them byte for byte |

The example includes constructors, overloaded arithmetic methods, a loop,
wide local instructions, both switch forms, native/abstract methods, an
exception handler, line/local-variable tables, and a raw unknown attribute.

The opcode matrix and constant-load fixture test encoding/structural
analysis. They do not claim executable stack/type correctness; Moss does not
execute classfiles or perform full JVM type verification.

The process-level integration tests generate malformed and maximum-budget
inputs in a process-identified, exclusively claimed directory under `target`.
They remove only files they created and then their empty directory.
